title: Oklahoma's 31-Game Winning Streak (1948-50) and How It Ended
question: How long was Oklahoma's winning streak before the 47-game run, and who ended it?
answer: Bud Wilkinson's Sooners won 31 straight games from October 1948 through the 1950 regular season. Kentucky, coached by Bear Bryant, ended it with a 13-7 win in the Sugar Bowl on Jan. 1, 1951.
summary: Before the famous 47-game run, Bud Wilkinson's Sooners won 31 straight from 1948 to 1950. Bear Bryant's Kentucky ended it 13-7 in the 1951 Sugar Bowl.
body: Oklahoma's 47-game winning streak gets most of the attention, but Bud Wilkinson's early teams built a remarkable run of their own. It began after the Sooners opened the 1948 season with a 20-17 loss at Santa Clara. Oklahoma then won its next ten games, including a 14-6 Sugar Bowl victory over North Carolina on Jan. 1, 1949.

The 1949 team went 11-0 and finished with a 35-0 Sugar Bowl win over LSU on Jan. 1, 1950. That added eleven wins to the streak. The 1950 Sooners went 10-0 in the regular season, including a 14-13 win over Texas in Dallas, and arrived in New Orleans ranked No. 1 with 31 straight victories, the longest run in the country at the time.

Kentucky, coached by Paul "Bear" Bryant, stood in the way on Jan. 1, 1951. Before 80,206 fans at Tulane Stadium, the Wildcats built a 13-0 lead, with quarterback Babe Parilli throwing a 22-yard touchdown pass early and Kentucky adding a short scoring run. Oklahoma answered late on a 17-yard touchdown pass from Billy Vessels to Merrill Green, but time ran short.

The loss did not cost Oklahoma its place in history. The Sooners had already been voted the 1950 national champions by the Associated Press at the end of the regular season, the program's first. Just a few years later, Wilkinson's team would begin a streak that grew even longer.
